text:
UPDATE: My last dollars spent here- EVER

I made a post last night about my package missing 7 of my 8 items I ordered. This was a $321.84 order I placed during the friends and family sale. I was told by two associates, one on chat, one on the phone and then a phone supervisor as well, that there was nothing they could do because the weight of the package showed as if all the products were in there (so this was obviously an inside job in a warehouse- IMO).

Anyway, I read through so many of your guys helpful comments, recommending chargebacks with my card, filing a complaint with BBB, messaging LinkedIn higher ups and Sephoras social media profiles, and continuing to call. I am very happy to say that a resolution has been made with this order. So in case anyone else has had this issue with no resolution yet, here is what I did. I filed a complaint with the BBB, and I listed the San Francisco location (I googled where their main office is and that location is what came up). I wrote in as much detail as possible what happened, I included photos of my package and the one item in it, I included the chat messages with Sephora where they said there is nothing they could do, and I included screenshots of the original order from the Sephora app showing what I was supposed to receive, the total spent, and the order number.

I filed this complaint at 11:55pm last night, got a confirmation email from the BBB this morning at 10:54am saying they had accepted this case and forwarded along to Sephora. Then today at 2:04pm I got an email from Sephora Client Relations saying they have seen the complaint with the BBB and have issued me a refund for $277.33 (the total minus the body lotion +tax for that item).

I still stand firm in my decision to not spend another penny at this store. The way I was treated was horrendous as someone who has been a loyal rouge member for many, many years and having to go through these lengths should not be necessary. So be warned, if you insist on shopping this store, do it in person. For me, I’ll stick with ordering directly from the brand’s websites. They have better deals anyway. Thank you all for your kind advice! I really appreciate you all!
label: opinion_complaint

text:
Tell me about your fav shine control products to use WITHOUT makeup? 🪄✨

[Advice]

I am a dew/glow chaser. I use my prescription Tret, I exfoliate, I brighten... and I skin flood and use barrier-repairing moisturizers and glowy Korean sunscreens. So, yeah, I love the glow.

But, occasionally, I'll find I'm looking a touch too shiny on somewhere like the nose or the very upper forehead. I am never going to be a full-on matte person, but I'm curious if y'all have any product recommendations that can help you take down the shine in a hyper-targeted area without going full on matte and without requiring makeup.

On days in which I'm wearing makeup, the combo of my Hourglass Veil Translucent Setting Powder and/or my Pat McGrath Blurring Under Eye Powder (which is also great for targeted placement anywhere on the face) will do the trick. But I don't want to be using those on non-makeup days.

I've been seeing these Korean lavender gel "powders" on my FYP later. They don't even actually look like traditional loose or pressed powder... but they seem designed for this type of thing.

Any suggestions? They don't have to be at Sephora. (Oh, and, I have a tan/medium complexion, so don't want something that will leave a grey/white cast, like the Laneige powder)

text:
Kosas soulgazer mascara vs. Ilia limitless lash mascara

I love clean formulas.

I've been using kosas for a while and it's pretty good. I have a lot of lashes though and I feel like it can't quite catch my inner corners lashes. It's a thicccc waxy formula so you lowkey need to wipe off the excess before applying it otherwise it's a gooey nightmare. It hold up well but I think by the end of the day it slowly goes down. But it's pretty good for what it does.

I bought ilia as a backup and haven't used it yet. I've seen some people saying ilia burns the shit out your eyes if you cry so I'm a little concerned about using that lmao... (I only buy mini mascaras cuz it dries out fast and cuz I throw it out every three months cuz I don't wanna get an allergic reaction)

*Apparently, they both have a peptide that can grow your lashes. Kosas brags about that on their mascara. Personally, I can't really tell but I think I've seen a little difference in growth.

For me I love a lot of length and volume I want to make it look like I got a lash lift so I'm wondering which one is better
